title: Current projects: Octet, Tahoe summit, book tour

blocks.x: I admire the work that you’ve both done and the fact that you could take some time out because I know you’re in the middle of a lot of things — a tour of the Brubeck Octet Project —

But we arrived in time to see the premier of it — Jon De Lucia — at the Wilton Library. The Wilton Library in Wilton, Connecticut has become kind of a new focal point — newish because it’s been going on for a few years, of Brubeck activity after the Brubeck Institute moved from the University of the Pacific to the East Coast and became directly under family control rather than, you know, kind of a coalition with the institution and so forth. So anyway that’s the octet. But I am moving on to the Brubeck Jazz Summit at © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

Lake Tahoe where I’ll be playing with Chris and Dan. And yeah, yeah, we are busy and we’re setting up a book tour for next year, April of next year. You know setting up a tour means you need kind of an anchor date and then you build things around it. So right now there’s too many moving parts but we know we’re going to be doing something at Jazz at Lincoln Center unless they can’t give us a venue, and if they can’t then we’ll do it at Juilliard or vice versa. But that agreement’s in place. And then we’re going out to Champaign-Urbana because that’s the University of Illinois Press and I’m a Wesleyan alum so we’ll do it at Wesleyan, Connecticut, and Emory University in Atlanta is interested. So you know who knows? But we’ll have a busy itinerary. And otherwise we’ll just do what old retired people do.
